llm.summary: This skill appears to be a local logging utility presented as a rating tool, so users could accidentally persist sensitive input on disk.

dimensions.detail: Persistent local logging and later search/export are disproportionate for a simple rating utility, especially because users may paste private prompts, secrets, or proprietary text into generic commands.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No separate installer or remote payload was found in the inspected artifact; runtime use creates a local data directory and files under the user's home directory.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Invocation language is broad, and commands such as run, check, analyze, generate, export, and status accept free-form input and save it locally without clear boundaries around appropriate data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The script creates ~/.local/share/rating and retains timestamped command content indefinitely, has no documented purge or opt-out path, and the documented RATING_DIR override is not honored by the script.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md describes star ratings, score calculations, ranking, and review management, but the script mostly implements generic commands that append arbitrary input to per-command log files.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this carefully before installing. Do not use it with secrets, private prompts, customer data, or proprietary text unless you are comfortable with that content being stored in local log files indefinitely. The package should document retention and deletion, honor its configurable data directory, and narrow its command behavior to real rating tasks before routine use.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: The scanner concern is supported in part: storage, history, search, and export are mentioned in SKILL.md, but the main description still frames the artifact as a rating system while the script behaves primarily as a generic local logger.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Supported: the description says 'everyday use' and 'Use when you need rating,' while the runtime command surface is broader than rating-specific work.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Supported: SKILL.md discloses local storage and timestamped activity logging, but does not describe retention, sensitivity risk, permissions, opt-out, or deletion.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Supported: scripts/script.sh creates ~/.local/share/rating and appends user-provided command content to log files.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Supported: the script's generic logging commands do not match the documented star rating, score calculation, ranking, and review-management purpose.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Supported: duplicate case labels mean export and status are handled by logging branches before the later helper implementations can be reached.
[SQP-2] expected: Partially supported: an export implementation exists that writes accumulated logs to json, csv, or txt files, which is a disclosed feature, but it increases retained-data copies and lacks confirmation or privacy guidance.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Supported: many pseudo-functional commands accept arbitrary input and append it to persistent logs, creating a broad capture surface unrelated to rating-specific behavior.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Supported: command inputs are written to local logs with timestamps and echoed back without an upfront warning at the point of use.
